title: Add gestures to the widget
line: Swiping two fingers left or right over the Media Player widget now goes to the previous or next track.
explanation: The Media Player widget's scroll handler treated horizontal scrolling the same as vertical scrolling, so a two-finger left/right swipe on a touchpad only changed the volume and there was no gesture for changing track. Two-finger up/down already changes the volume, which covers that part of the request. The change makes horizontal scrolling go to the previous or next track instead: once per touchpad swipe (the swipe is tracked through Qt's scroll phases, so a long swipe never skips several tracks) and once per notch on a tilting mouse wheel. It also works on the media icon in the system tray, which uses the same compact representation.

commits.message:
applets/mediacontroller: change track with horizontal scrolling

Horizontal scrolling over the widget used to change the volume like the
vertical one. It now goes to the previous or next track, once per swipe
on a touchpad or once per notch on a tilting mouse wheel.

BUG: 460588

media.caption: Before: scrolling left twice and right twice over the panel widget only changes the volume (player log: 6 SetVolume calls); the track stays "Track 3".
After: the same scrolls go to Track 2, Track 1, then back to Track 2 and Track 3 (player log: Previous, Previous, Next, Next; volume unchanged).

reviews.text: Mapping horizontal scrolling over Media Player's CompactRepresentation to previous/next track (one per touchpad swipe or tilt-wheel notch) while keeping vertical scrolling for volume is a sensible, clean way to deliver swipe controls using existing scroll events. However, the state machine in onWheel has edge cases with missed ScrollEnd events breaking tilt wheels, diagonal touchpad swipes triggering cross-axis actions, and potential ScrollMomentum double-skips.
changes: Reset swiped and horizontalWheelDelta on Qt.NoScrollPhase (and before the mpris2Model.currentPlayer === null early return), because if a touchpad swipe leaves the widget before Qt.ScrollEnd arrives, swiped stays true and permanently blocks subsequent tilting mouse-wheel events.

Lock each phased touchpad gesture to a single axis (horizontal track skip vs vertical volume) and reset wheelDelta on gesture boundaries, so diagonal finger drift during a vertical volume scroll cannot accumulate horizontalWheelDelta and skip tracks, and vertical drift after a horizontal track skip cannot alter the volume.
Ignore Qt.ScrollMomentum events for track changes (or avoid resetting swiped on ScrollEnd before momentum finishes) so inertial momentum events cannot trigger an unintended second track skip.

reviews.text: Mapping horizontal scrolling to previous/next is a sensible, contained way to get the swipe gesture without QTBUG-92086. Using scroll phases to skip only one track per swipe and keeping the finger direction under natural scrolling is careful work, and the video plus the player log back it up. But the reporter asked for three gestures and the commit says BUG: while the two-finger hold for play/pause is not done; the notes only point to middle-click. It is also a new, master-only feature, so the 'no new strings for backport' reasoning doesn't hold: the tooltip still says only 'Scroll to adjust volume', so the new gesture can't be discovered.
changes: Either provide a touchpad play/pause gesture the reporter can use, or switch to CCBUG: 460588 and leave the bug open (or narrowed) for the hold gesture that needs upstream support.
Update the compact tooltip to mention that horizontal scrolling changes the track (new string on master).
